spec_match.rationale: Exercises AudioContextRenderSizeCategory 'hardware' vs 'default' crossed with latencyHint, reading renderQuantumSize, sampleRate, baseLatency and outputLatency — the exact negotiation surface the spec defines.

interactive.rationale: Negotiate button builds four real contexts and fills the table, verdict panel and copyable report; copy button writes to the clipboard with a labelled manual fallback.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Card promises an honest per-device negotiation report including the 'no difference here' outcome, which is exactly what renders (and what this sandbox shows).

edge_cases.rationale: Suspended-context readings are labelled and clipboard failure is handled, but the 'hardware differs from default' verdict branch could not be exercised in this environment (null audio sink always grants 128) — it is code-reviewed only.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5078190552907776, the 'hardware' enum spec anchor, and the explainer's Android 192-frame motivating example.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite covers the attribute and enum contracts; the platform-buffer table is explicitly labelled as orientation context, not assertions.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Real-time CDP run on headless Chromium 141+flag: four contexts negotiated (128 each, baseLatency 10.00 ms interactive vs 23.22 ms playback), honest same-as-default verdict shown, report generated and copied; console/network clean except the environmental fonts failure. Not chrome-devtools-mcp (unavailable here).

telemetry_health.rationale: hhr-support asserts the fallback branch separately and hhr-negotiated only passes when the granted quantum was actually readable.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; the secondary copy button overrides background AND color together; accent-blue/emerald verdict emphasis on paper background meets AA at bold weight.

accessibility.rationale: Native buttons, captioned tables with row/column headers, aria-live polite status, and the report exposed as a labelled pre block.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at 360x740 DPR3 touch and 1280x1400: tables and the report pre scroll inside their containers, zero document overflow, 44px buttons.

openQuestions.title: Capture a device where 'hardware' genuinely negotiates a non-128 quantum
openQuestions.detail: The differs-branch verdict (emerald) and its report wording have not been observed live — this sandbox's null audio sink grants 128 for every hint. Run the page on Android (AAudio burst 192/240) or a Windows WASAPI machine with Chrome 153 and confirm the verdict, duration math and copyable report for a non-128 grant.

openQuestions.title: outputLatency reads 0.00 ms on the null sink
openQuestions.detail: outputLatency is reported honestly but is 0.00 ms in this environment, so its suspended-vs-running annotation has limited coverage; re-check on real output hardware.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use semantic tables (caption, th scope), native buttons, and live-region announcements for async outcomes.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Both tables have captions and scoped headers; row headers carry the context options; negotiation and copy outcomes are announced via role=status aria-live=polite.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Keep wide tabular content scrolling in its own overflow container and let control rows wrap instead of fixing widths.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Both tables and the report pre use overflow-x:auto wrappers; the button row is flex-wrap:wrap; code tokens wrap with overflow-wrap:anywhere.

guidanceConsulted.query: button triggers async API call show pending state disable and announce result to screen readers
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Disable the trigger during the async action and announce the result rather than relying on visual change alone.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Negotiate disables while running and re-enables on completion; the copy button stays disabled until a report exists; results are announced in the status region.

summary: Honest per-device negotiation report for renderSizeHint 'hardware': four contexts across the latencyHint extremes, granted values, latency readouts, a plain-language verdict (including the no-difference case this sandbox produces), a copyable report, and a clearly-labelled typical-buffer orientation table.
